nodes.label: Request Flow Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The flow deliberately spans several modules: main.py routes and maps FailureType to message + error_type; lookup.py orchestrates cache -> negative cache -> provider -> record; browser.py owns the Browser and yields a fresh context; scraper.py runs named Playwright steps with block detection and parsing; cache.py stores only successes; failures.py stores failures and the negative cache; stats.py de-duplicates alerts into telegram_notify.py.

nodes.label: Module-Level settings Singleton
nodes.rationale: app/config.py builds settings from .env at import time and it is read at call time rather than captured, so tests override behaviour with monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "field", value). Changing database_path requires connection.reset_for_tests() because the connection is cached in a module global. Telegram credentials must come from .env only; defaults are empty strings and a regression test asserts they carry no credentials.

nodes.label: Failure Taxonomy (FailureType)
nodes.rationale: FailureType in schemas.py is the spine of the design: the original code collapsed every failure into a bare None, making a blocked scraper indistinguishable from a nonexistent address. Every failure path must return a classified LookupOutcome carrying reason, step and URL.

nodes.label: Invariant: Only FailureType.NOT_FOUND May Be Negatively Cached
nodes.norm_label: invariant: only failuretype.not_found may be negatively cached
nodes.rationale: Negatively caching blocked/timeout/error would freeze a transient outage into a permanent wrong answer; only a genuinely nonexistent address is a stable negative fact.

nodes.label: Named Playwright Scraper Steps
nodes.rationale: scraper.py labels each step (goto_home, fill_search, await_autocomplete, click_suggestion, await_result_nav, extract_html, parse) so a failure reports exactly where it broke instead of only that it broke.

nodes.label: not_found vs timeout Classification
nodes.rationale: _classify_missing_autocomplete decides the distinction: if no suggestion appeared but the page is otherwise healthy (search box present, text still in it, no block markers) the address is genuinely unknown; otherwise the scraper is at fault. detect_block checks HTTP status, off-site redirects and content markers and runs before any fallback to a timeout classification, so a block is never mislabelled.

nodes.label: BC Assessment Service
nodes.rationale: A FastAPI service returning BC Assessment property data for a formatted address: SQLite cache first, then a Playwright scrape of bcassessment.ca parsed with BeautifulSoup. Consumed by BlueNest's BCAssessmentClient, deployed on a Linux VPS under systemd behind nginx.

nodes.label: graphify Knowledge Graph of the Repo
nodes.norm_label: graphify knowledge graph of the repo
nodes.rationale: The repo is mapped as a graphify knowledge graph in graphify-out/; the graph is treated as the map of the codebase, queried with graphify query (BFS, broad context), graphify path (what links two things) and graphify explain (plain-language node summary). On this machine graphify runs from the Python 3.13 install, with the interpreter path cached in graphify-out/.graphify_python and the graphify CLI on PATH.

nodes.label: graphify-out Outputs
nodes.rationale: An update regenerates all of them: graph.json (raw graph data, 422 nodes / 892 edges at last full build), graph.html (interactive graph for a browser), GRAPH_REPORT.md (audit report of god nodes, communities, surprising edges) and manifest.json (per-file hashes, which is what makes --update incremental). If graphify-out/ is ever deleted, a full /graphify . is required rather than --update, because there is no manifest to diff against.

nodes.label: FailureType as Dominant Bridge Node
nodes.rationale: FailureType is the graph's dominant bridge node (betweenness 0.276, 47 edges, spanning seven communities). Anything touching it reaches most of the service, so the graph must be checked before assuming a change there is local.

nodes.label: Graph-First Workflow Before Any Change
nodes.rationale: Do not start from a blind file search: query the existing graph first to find what a change touches and what depends on it. The graph reveals reach that file search does not, which is why it precedes editing rather than following it.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Instructs but Does Not Enforce
nodes.norm_label: claude.md instructs but does not enforce
nodes.rationale: The graphify section instructs Claude and Claude honours it when it reads the file, but nothing mechanically stops a change from landing without the graph update. For a hard guarantee the recommendation is graphify's post-commit hook, so every commit rebuilds the graph automatically.

nodes.label: Invariant: Only Valid Results Reach assessment_cache
nodes.norm_label: invariant: only valid results reach assessment_cache
nodes.rationale: Anything without total_value is a failure and belongs in failed_lookups, not assessment_cache. cache_set enforces this defensively rather than trusting callers.

nodes.label: Mandatory Post-Change graphify --update
nodes.rationale: Running /graphify . --update after any change to code or docs is not optional and not deferred to end of session, because a graph describing deleted or renamed symbols is worse than no graph: it is confidently wrong. Code-only changes skip semantic extraction entirely (AST only, no LLM, no tokens) so there is no reason to batch or skip; edits to CLAUDE.md, README.md, CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md, TEST_RESULTS.md or how-it-works.html do cost tokens. A change means any edit to app/, scripts/ or tests/, any added/renamed/moved/deleted file, or any edit to those docs — renames and deletions matter most, since --update prunes the old nodes and nothing else will.

nodes.label: Single Source of Schema DDL in db/connection.py
nodes.norm_label: single source of schema ddl in db/connection.py
nodes.rationale: db/connection.py owns both the single shared SQLite connection and the schema DDL so runtime and scripts/setup_db.py can never drift. The schema is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS throughout and re-applied on connect, which is what lets setup_db.py double as the migration for databases predating failed_lookups.

nodes.label: SCRAP/ Virtualenv Convention
nodes.rationale: The virtualenv is named SCRAP/ rather than .venv/ to match the systemd unit and the README. On the Windows dev machine python is not on PATH, so the py launcher (Python 3.13) is used; Playwright is only needed for LOOKUP_PROVIDER=live and the test suite never launches a browser.

nodes.label: Production Hang and False Property-Not-Found Outage
nodes.norm_label: production hang and false property-not-found outage
nodes.rationale: The service previously hung and returned false "Property not found" until a systemd timer restarted it every 2 hours. The five invariants exist as the fixes; violating any of them reintroduces the outage. The README documents the full root cause.

nodes.label: Invariant: Never Reuse a Page or BrowserContext Across Lookups
nodes.norm_label: invariant: never reuse a page or browsercontext across lookups
nodes.rationale: Reusing a page left the previous property's DOM in place; the readiness check then matched that stale markup and cached the previous property's values under the new address. browser_manager.lookup_context() is the only sanctioned way to obtain a page and always tears the context down, making the defect impossible rather than merely unlikely.

nodes.label: Invariant: Acquire bc_rate_limiter Before _scrape_lock
nodes.rationale: Rate-limit waits can last up to an hour at the hourly cap; holding the scrape semaphore through one blocked every queued request. Acquiring the rate limiter outside the lock is the direct fix for the hang.

nodes.label: Mock Lookup Provider
nodes.rationale: _mock_lookup in lookup.py derives values from a hash of the address so distinct addresses yield distinct figures; magic tokens NOWHERE/INVALID/DOESNOTEXIST produce not_found and BLOCKED produces blocked. Because the mock cannot exhibit the stale-page defect, the real regression test for it is scripts/load_test.py --mode stale against a live server, asserting distinct addresses never return the same total_value.

nodes.label: Autouse Test Fixtures in conftest.py
nodes.rationale: Two autouse fixtures give every test a throwaway SQLite database and silenced/reset alerting; the client fixture sets LOOKUP_PROVIDER=mock so the full request path runs without Playwright or network.

nodes.label: Invariant: /address Response Shape Is a Contract
nodes.norm_label: invariant: /address response shape is a contract
nodes.rationale: BlueNest depends on the exact bytes: the success shape and the literal string "Property not found" must stay byte-for-byte identical. error_type may only be added, never substituted for existing fields.
